gastro.intro_sub: A handy guide to know what to order at the market or restaurant, no surprises.

juane.queEs: The king of Amazonian dishes. Rice seasoned with palillo (wild turmeric) and spices, with hard-boiled egg and a piece of hen, wrapped and cooked in bijao leaves.
juane.comoComer: Unwrap the leaf by hand and enjoy it with cocona chili sauce and fried ripe plantain.
juane.precioAprox: S/ 7.00 at the market • S/ 25.00 at a restaurant

tacacho.queEs: Balls of mashed green plantain, roasted or fried, mixed with pork lard and crackling, served with cecina (smoked pork) and handmade Loreto chorizo.
tacacho.comoComer: Shred the cecina and pair each piece with a bite of steaming tacacho.

paiche.queEs: The world's largest scaled freshwater fish. Its flesh is white, firm, free of small bones, with a mild, refined flavor.
paiche.comoComer: Grilled, as crispy fried chunks, or in Amazonian ceviche with charapita chili.

patarashca.queEs: Amazonian fish seasoned with sachaculantro (wild coriander), onion and sweet pepper, wrapped in bijao leaves and slowly grilled over charcoal.
patarashca.comoComer: The leaf seals in all the fish's natural juices, with no added fat needed.
patarashca.precioAprox: S/ 10.00 at the market • S/ 30.00 at a restaurant

chonta.queEs: Thin strips from the heart of the Amazonian palm. Fresh and crunchy, served cold with lime, salt and oil.
chonta.comoComer: The perfect starter to beat the jungle's humid heat.

suri.queEs: Edible beetle larva that grows inside fallen aguaje palm trunks. Rich in natural oils and protein.
suri.comoComer: Grilled on skewers over charcoal with a pinch of salt. Crispy outside and soft inside, a bit like fried chicken skin.

camucamu.queEs: Iconic fruits. Camu camu has 40 times more vitamin C than orange; aguaje is a fleshy palm fruit packed with beta-carotene.
camucamu.comoComer: In iced juices, shaved ice or homemade popsicles to cool down in the afternoon.
camucamu.precioAprox: S/ 3.00 to S/ 6.00 per iced glass

1.descripcionCorta: White-sand Tunchi Playa beach, rescued animals and giant paiche fish.
1.descripcionLarga: An iconic tourist complex and zoo around Lake Quistococha. It features the famous Tunchi Playa, a natural white-sand freshwater beach, breeding ponds for giant paiche (Arapaima gigas), manatees, dolphins, rescued wild cats and botanical trails through the forest.
1.recomendaciones: Bring a swimsuit for the lagoon, mosquito repellent and sunscreen. Try the fresh fish at the local kiosks on the lakeshore.
1.audio: Welcome to the Quistococha Complex. This beautiful dark-water lagoon, surrounded by lush vegetation, is home to rescued species such as the Amazonian manatee and the mighty paiche. Enjoy Tunchi Playa, a natural white-sand beach in the heart of the Amazon.
1.acceso: Mototaxi or shared minibus from Plaza 28 de Julio (~30 min)
1.direccion: Iquitos-Nauta Highway Km 14.5, San Juan Bautista

2.descripcionCorta: White-sand varillal forests and endemic birds such as the Iquitos gnatcatcher.
2.descripcionLarga: Famous for its varillal forests growing on white sand, with an astonishing concentration of bird and plant species found nowhere else on Earth. Home to the Iquitos gnatcatcher (Polioptila clemencei) and the black titi monkey.
2.recomendaciones: A certified local guide is mandatory. Bring trekking or rubber boots, a light raincoat and binoculars for birdwatching.
2.audio: Allpahuayo Mishana is a world-class ecological treasure. Its white quartz-sand soil creates a varillal ecosystem unique in the Amazon, where birds live that exist only in this protected forest.
2.acceso: Car / shared minibus along the Nauta highway + hike along trails

3.descripcionCorta: The Amazonian Venice: traditional medicine, ayahuasca vines and houses on stilts.
3.descripcionLarga: A vibrant community built on balsa-wood stilts and rafts that float when the Itaya River rises and rest on land when it recedes. On dry land lies Pasaje Paquito, the hub of Amazonian traditional medicine, where roots, barks such as cat's claw, copaiba oil and sacred ayahuasca brews are sold.
3.recomendaciones: Best visited in the morning. Go with a local guide or a trusted boatman. Watch your belongings and ask permission before photographing residents.
3.audio: Belén, known as the Venice of the Amazon. During the rainy months, houses and schools float freely on the water. Here in Pasaje Paquito, the ancestral wisdom of shamans and healers from the entire basin comes together.
3.acceso: On foot to the riverbank, then peke-peke boat on the Itaya River
3.costo: Boat ride S/ 20 - 30 per hour, negotiable
3.distancia: On the eastern bank of Iquitos (1.5 km from downtown)
3.direccion: Down to the Itaya River, Belén District

4.descripcionCorta: Amazon Rescue Center dedicated to rehabilitating manatees and wildlife.
4.descripcionLarga: A pioneering institution in the Peruvian Amazon dedicated to rescuing, rehabilitating and releasing Amazonian manatees (Trichechus inunguis), giant otters, taricaya turtles and monkeys that fell victim to illegal trafficking. Visitors can bottle-feed them under veterinary supervision.
4.recomendaciones: Great for families. Strictly follow the rule of not touching animals without authorization from the biologists.
4.audio: CREA is a sanctuary of hope for Amazonian wildlife. Here, scientists and volunteers bring orphaned manatees back to life and raise awareness among riverside communities about protecting biodiversity.

5.descripcionCorta: Departure point for peke-peke boats, grilled suri grubs and doncella fish.
5.descripcionLarga: The traditional port in the north of the city on the banks of the blackwater Nanay River. It is the departure point for the Momón River, Padre Cocha and the Serpentarium. Its famous food boulevard offers grilled suri skewers, fried doncella fish, cecina with tacacho and aguaje juice.
5.recomendaciones: Dare to try a suri skewer fresh off the charcoal. Hire boats that carry proper life jackets.
5.audio: Bellavista Nanay is where the city meets the rivers. Here you can smell wood smoke and roasted plantain, and hear the hum of peke-peke motors gliding over the calm dark waters of the Nanay.
5.costo: Free entry. Peke-peke boats from S/ 15 - 40
5.distancia: 5 km north of Plaza de Armas
5.direccion: End of Av. La Marina, Punchana

6.descripcionCorta: Muddy adventure through bogs and secondary jungle on all-terrain ATVs.
6.descripcionLarga: An adrenaline circuit through rough trails, jungle stream crossings and clay mud pits. Led by expert instructors in jungle mechanics, with stops at viewpoints over primary vegetation.
6.recomendaciones: A full change of clothes is essential, plus sneakers you don't mind getting dirty, repellent and goggles to protect against mud.
6.audio: Get ready for extreme excitement in the jungle. The ATV route will test your skills driving over Amazonian mud, roots and wild trails surrounded by dense vegetation.

7.descripcionCorta: A flashlight expedition in the dark to spot tarantulas, frogs and snakes.
7.descripcionLarga: The jungle transforms when the sun goes down. A guided walk with biologists and native guides tracking burrowing tarantulas, Amazon tree boas, poison dart frogs and nocturnal mammals, to the chorus of Amazonian insects.
7.recomendaciones: Bring a powerful flashlight (preferably a headlamp), long waterproof pants, a long-sleeved shirt and strong repellent.
7.audio: When night falls in the jungle, 80% of the wildlife wakes up. On this walk you will feel the pulse of the living jungle under the stars, observing fascinating creatures in their nocturnal habitat.
7.acceso: By 4x4 vehicle or boat depending on the season

8.nombre: Al Frío y al Fuego (Floating Restaurant)
8.descripcionCorta: Floating restaurant with a pool, signature Amazonian cuisine, paiche and gourmet cecina.
8.descripcionLarga: An emblematic floating restaurant with a central pool on the waters of the Itaya River. It serves signature Amazonian cuisine with avant-garde presentations of grilled paiche, doncella tiradito with cocona sauce and camu camu pisco cocktails.
8.recomendaciones: Book for sunset (5:30 PM) to watch the sun go down over the river with an exotic drink.
8.audio: Al Frío y al Fuego is the ultimate expression of contemporary Amazonian cuisine, a floating oasis blending tradition and innovation with panoramic views of the vast river.
8.acceso: Free private boat from the Calle Próspero pier
8.distancia: On the Itaya River (facing the city)
8.direccion: On the Itaya River (boarding at Calle Próspero, block 1)

9.descripcionCorta: Riverside terrace with camu camu juices, fresh chonta salad and specialty coffee.
9.descripcionLarga: A cozy terrace on the historic boardwalk with prime views of the Itaya River. Specializes in fusion cuisine, jungle vegetarian options, fresh chonta (heart of palm) salads and Amazonian cocktails.
9.recomendaciones: Order the fresh morning camu camu smoothie or the shredded cecina sandwich.
9.audio: Relax in the river breeze at Dawn on the Amazon, a favorite spot for travelers from around the world to enjoy organic coffee and fresh chonta while watching the boats go by.
9.acceso: On foot on the downtown boardwalk
9.direccion: Malecón Maldonado 185, facing the Itaya River

10.descripcionCorta: A tribute to the rubber era: classic tacacho with cecina and ribs with charapita chili.
10.descripcionLarga: Named after the famous film and rubber baron, set in a historic colonial-style mansion facing the river. Generous traditional dishes such as tacacho with cecina and homemade chorizo, paiche ceviche and lomo saltado with chonta.
10.recomendaciones: Grab an outdoor table at night to enjoy the live music and the boardwalk breeze.
10.audio: The living history of Iquitos and the rubber boom at Fitzcarrald. Its kitchen honors age-old ingredients with the unmistakable flavor of charapita chili.
10.acceso: On foot on the central boardwalk
10.direccion: Malecón Maldonado, corner of Calle Napo

11.descripcionCorta: Rice juanes in bijao leaves, charcoal-grilled patarashca, carachama chilcano and masato.
11.descripcionLarga: The beating heart of Iquitos' popular cuisine. Lively stalls where local cooks prepare steaming juanes wrapped in bijao leaves, patarashca (Amazonian fish grilled in leaves), nourishing carachama chilcano soup and fermented cassava masato.
11.recomendaciones: Go early (7:00 to 10:00 AM). Bring cash in small bills and try the patarashca fresh off the embers.
11.audio: Belén Market is the cradle of Loreto's popular flavors. Here the aromas of bijao leaves, charcoal and wild coriander tell the story of the Amazonian farmer and fisherman.

101.descripcionCorta: The historic heart of Iquitos, facing the Main Church and Gustave Eiffel's Iron House.
101.descripcionLarga: The main square of Iquitos, surrounded by buildings from the rubber era. It is home to the Heroes' Obelisk, circular fountains lit up at night, and right next to the historic Iron House designed by Gustave Eiffel.
101.recomendaciones: Perfect for a stroll at sunset, an aguaje or camu camu ice cream, and photos of the Main Church.
101.audio: The Plaza de Armas of Iquitos is the heart of Loreto's capital, a witness to the splendor of the rubber boom and the starting point of every Amazon expedition.
101.acceso: On foot in the city center

102.descripcionCorta: The city's balcony over the Itaya River, with colonial mansions clad in tiles imported from Portugal.
102.descripcionLarga: Built in the late 19th century during the rubber boom. Its tree-lined promenade offers stunning panoramic views of the Itaya River and its confluence with the Amazon. It is flanked by mansions decorated with tiles brought from Europe.
102.recomendaciones: Visit between 5:30 PM and 8:00 PM to watch the Amazonian sunset in the cool breeze.
102.audio: Malecón Tarapacá is the legendary viewpoint of Iquitos. From here, the old rubber barons watched transatlantic steamers loaded with rubber set sail for Europe.
102.acceso: On foot from the Plaza de Armas toward the river

103.descripcionCorta: The largest square in Iquitos, surrounded by shops and home to the shared-minibus stop for Nauta and Quistococha.
103.descripcionLarga: The city's largest civic square, with fountains and a children's playground. It is the key transport hub where you catch shared minibuses and mototaxis to the Iquitos-Nauta Highway, Quistococha and CREA.
103.recomendaciones: The key spot for catching affordable land transport to the south of the city.
103.audio: Plaza 28 de Julio, the hub of local transport and a favorite place for Iquitos families to relax and play.
103.direccion: Av. Grau block 4 at Calle Bermúdez

104.descripcionCorta: The busiest shopping street in Iquitos, with banks, agencies and stores.
104.descripcionLarga: The main street of the Iquitos economy. It has the largest number of ATMs, official currency exchange offices, travel agencies, pharmacies and Amazonian souvenir shops.
104.recomendaciones: Use the ATMs on this street during the day for greater safety.
104.audio: Jirón Próspero is the backbone of commerce and urban life in Iquitos, linking the Plaza de Armas with the Belén district.
104.acceso: On foot from Plaza de Armas

501.descripcionCorta: Rent your own motorbike to get around Iquitos freely and ride out along the Iquitos-Nauta Highway.
501.descripcionLarga: Alquiler de Motos Leo offers well-maintained motorbikes for full-day rental, ideal for exploring downtown Iquitos at your own pace or heading out on the Iquitos-Nauta Highway. Includes a helmet and a short riding briefing.
501.recomendaciones: Bring your driver's license and a copy of your ID for the security deposit.
501.audio: Alquiler de Motos Leo, at the corner of Morona and Tacna streets, gives you the freedom to explore Iquitos and its surroundings on your own motorbike.
501.direccion: Corner of Calle Morona and Tacna, Downtown Iquitos

502.descripcionCorta: An iron-plate building attributed to Gustave Eiffel, a symbol of the rubber era.
502.descripcionLarga: Built with iron plates brought from Europe during the rubber boom, the Iron House is one of the most recognizable architectural symbols of Iquitos and the Peruvian Amazon.
502.recomendaciones: Visit during the day to photograph the details of the metal plates, and combine it with a stroll around the Plaza de Armas.
502.audio: The Iron House is an iron testimony to the rubber splendor that turned Iquitos into a cosmopolitan city in the middle of the jungle.
502.acceso: On foot in the city center

503.descripcionCorta: A collection of crafts, clothing and ritual objects from the Indigenous peoples of the Peruvian Amazon.
503.descripcionLarga: A museum bringing together original pieces from various Amazonian peoples (Bora, Huitoto, Shipibo and others), with explanations of their worldview, ceremonial dress and everyday objects.
503.recomendaciones: Allow an hour for the visit and check out the handicraft shop at the exit.
503.audio: The Museum of Amazonian Indigenous Cultures brings visitors closer to the worldview of the original peoples of Loreto.

504.descripcionCorta: A former rubber-baron mansion with a Portuguese-tile facade, now a boutique hotel.
504.descripcionLarga: One of the most elegant mansions of the rubber era, with tiles brought from Portugal and Italy. Today it operates as a boutique hotel and preserves much of its original architecture.
504.recomendaciones: Ideal for photographing the facade at sunset, along with the other mansions on Malecón Tarapacá.
504.audio: Casa Morey preserves in its tiles the luxury that rubber brought to the banks of the Amazon River.
504.costo: Free access to the facade / boutique hotel

505.descripcionCorta: A sanctuary where rescued monkeys live in semi-freedom surrounded by flooded forest.
505.descripcionLarga: A refuge on an Amazon island where different species of monkeys rescued from wildlife trafficking live together in a flooded-forest setting. Visitors can observe and interact with them up close under supervision.
505.recomendaciones: Bring sunscreen and repellent, and don't feed the monkeys without the guide's permission.
505.audio: Monkey Island is a second-chance refuge for rescued primates in the heart of the Amazon.
505.acceso: Boat from the pier (approx. 45 min - 1 h)
505.direccion: Isla de los Monos, Amazon River

506.descripcionCorta: An Amazonian butterfly farm that is also home to rescued animals such as Pancho the jaguar.
506.descripcionLarga: Pilpintuwasi ('House of Butterflies' in Quechua) breeds dozens of Amazonian butterfly species and also shelters other rescued animals: jaguars, tapirs, monkeys and birds, on a guided tour along jungle trails.
506.recomendaciones: Combine the visit with Bellavista Nanay and bring a camera: butterflies are most active when the sun is out.
506.audio: Pilpintuwasi is a sanctuary where the Amazon protects its butterflies and the wildlife left homeless by illegal trafficking.
506.distancia: ~15 min by boat from Bellavista Nanay
506.direccion: Padre Cocha, across from Bellavista Nanay
506.tarifaDesdePlaza: S/ 5.00 - S/ 7.00 to Bellavista Nanay + boat

507.descripcionCorta: Panoramic view over the Nanay River, perfect for an Amazonian sunset.
507.descripcionLarga: Peru's longest bridge crosses the Nanay River and links Iquitos with the northern communities. From its viewpoint you can see the river, the flooded forest and the boats arriving at Bellavista Nanay, with vividly colored sunsets.
507.recomendaciones: Go at sunset and bring repellent and water. Arrange the return trip or waiting time with your mototaxi driver.
507.audio: The Nanay Bridge connects Iquitos with the far bank of the river. From here, the horizon of jungle and water turns orange every evening.
507.direccion: Bridge over the Nanay River, north Iquitos

508.descripcionCorta: A 1906 steamship from the rubber era, turned into a floating museum.
508.descripcionLarga: The Ayapua is a ship built in Germany in the early 20th century that sailed the Amazon during the rubber boom. Today it is a floating museum showing how people lived and traded in the Amazon of that era.
508.recomendaciones: Combine it with the boardwalk and the Iron House. The visit takes about 45 minutes.
508.audio: Aboard the Ayapua we travel back to the rubber era, when steamships linked Iquitos with Europe and the river was the only highway.
508.acceso: On foot or a short mototaxi ride from the Plaza de Armas
508.direccion: Plaza Castilla, near the Iquitos boardwalk

600.nombre: Coronel FAP Francisco Secada Vignetta International Airport
600.descripcionCorta: Iquitos' only air gateway: the city has no road to the rest of Peru.
600.descripcionLarga: The main airport of Loreto, with daily flights to Lima and other cities. Outside you will find mototaxis and taxis; agree on the fare before getting in.
600.recomendaciones: Carry cash in soles for the transfer and agree on the price before getting in.
600.acceso: Mototaxi or taxi along Av. Quiñones (20-30 min)
600.costo: Mototaxi to downtown approx. S/ 15 - S/ 20
600.horario: Depends on flights, approx. 5:00 AM - 11:00 PM
600.direccion: Av. José Abelardo Quiñones km 6, San Juan Bautista

601.descripcionCorta: Bank with ATMs on the main shopping street downtown.
601.descripcionLarga: Several banks and ATMs are concentrated on Jr. Próspero. Withdraw soles here; in Iquitos almost everything is paid in cash.
601.recomendaciones: Withdraw during the day and put your money away before leaving the ATM.
601.acceso: On foot from the Plaza de Armas
601.costo: Foreign cards may be charged a withdrawal fee
601.horario: Branch Mon-Fri 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM, Saturday morning; ATMs approx. 24 h

602.descripcionCorta: The region's main public hospital, with 24-hour emergency care.
602.descripcionLarga: Loreto's referral hospital. It provides emergency care, consultations and inpatient services.
602.recomendaciones: Bring your ID and travel insurance.
602.costo: Public care, fees depend on the service

603.descripcionCorta: Adventist private clinic with 24-hour emergency care.
603.descripcionLarga: One of the best-known private clinics in Iquitos, with emergency care, consultations and a laboratory.
603.recomendaciones: Check whether your travel insurance has an agreement with them.
603.acceso: Short mototaxi ride from downtown (5 min)
603.costo: Private clinic, consultations from approx. S/ 60

604.descripcionCorta: Peruvian social security hospital with 24-hour emergency care.
604.descripcionLarga: EsSalud hospital for insured people. In serious emergencies it treats anyone.
604.recomendaciones: If you are not insured, choose the Regional Hospital or a private clinic.
604.costo: For EsSalud members; serious emergencies are treated

605.descripcionCorta: Buy a Peruvian prepaid SIM card with mobile data.
605.descripcionLarga: Claro carrier store on the main shopping street. You need your passport to buy a SIM card.
605.recomendaciones: Bring your passport: SIM registration is mandatory.
605.acceso: On foot from the Plaza de Armas

606.descripcionCorta: Prepaid SIM cards and top-ups from Movistar.
606.descripcionLarga: Movistar carrier store downtown. You need your passport to buy a SIM card.
606.recomendaciones: Bring your passport: SIM registration is mandatory.
606.acceso: On foot from the Plaza de Armas

607.nombre: Money changers on Jr. Próspero and Jr. Putumayo
607.descripcionCorta: Area with street money changers and exchange offices for dollars and euros.
607.descripcionLarga: Around Jr. Próspero and Jr. Putumayo there are money changers in vests and exchange offices. Count the money in front of them.
607.recomendaciones: Prefer exchange offices with a storefront and check the bills you receive.
607.acceso: On foot from the Plaza de Armas
607.direccion: Corner of Jr. Próspero and Jr. Putumayo, next to the Plaza de Armas

permisos.ubicacion_explicacion: To draw the route from where you are, SelvaGuide needs your location only while you use the app. We do not store or share it. If you prefer not to share it, we will calculate the route from the Plaza de Armas.
permisos.ubicacion_bloqueada: Location is turned off for SelvaGuide. You can turn it on in your phone settings. Meanwhile, we will calculate the route from the Plaza de Armas.

privacidad.intro: SelvaGuide respects your privacy and complies with Peru's Personal Data Protection Law No. 29733. Here we explain which data we use and why.
privacidad.datos_texto: Only what the app needs to work: your location while you plan a route, the photos you choose to upload and, if you sign in, your name and email.
privacidad.ubicacion_texto: Used only while the app is open, to calculate the route and fare. It is not stored on our servers or used in the background. You can deny it and the app keeps working.
privacidad.fotos_texto: Requested only when you attach a photo to a review. Photos you publish are visible to other travelers.
privacidad.cuenta_texto: You can use the app as a guest. If you sign in with Apple or Google, we store your name, email, language and bookings to provide the service.
privacidad.terceros_texto: To calculate routes we send the origin and destination coordinates to OpenStreetMap (OSRM), and we check the Iquitos weather on Open-Meteo. We never sell your data.
privacidad.derechos_texto: You can request access, correction or deletion of your data at any time, and withdraw permissions from your phone settings.
privacidad.contacto_texto: For any question about your data, write to us from the Help section of the app.

bienvenida.subtitulo: The essentials for your first hours in the city.
bienvenida.clima_d: Hot and humid all year, between 26 and 32 °C. Rain comes suddenly: bring a light raincoat, sunscreen and insect repellent.
bienvenida.moneda_d: Prices are in soles (S/). Almost everything is paid in cash; there are ATMs and banks downtown, especially on Jr. Próspero.
bienvenida.moverse_d: Mototaxis are the main transport. There are no meters: agree on the fare before getting in. Iquitos has no road to the rest of Peru; you can only arrive by plane or boat.
bienvenida.evitar_d: Unlicensed guides who approach you on the street, touching or feeding wild animals, and drinking tap water.

nav.error_abrir: The navigation app could not be opened. Check that it is installed.
